Calcédoine rubanée : quartz microcristal: Banded chalcedony: microcrystalline quartz in concentric, porous layers. It is the stone that has been dyed since ancient times, blue, green, red or black.
Agrégat microcristallin de quartz : lect: Microcrystalline quartz aggregate: diffuse reading, uniaxial positive in polarized light.
Pas de spectre net ; une teinture éventu: No clear spectrum; any dye gives its own bands.
Bandes concentriques de calcédoine, parf: Concentric bands of chalcedony, sometimes a cavity lined with quartz crystals (geode).
Un béryl bleu à bleu-vert pâle, coloré p: A pale blue to blue-green beryl, colored by iron, like sea water. It is the blue variety of beryl, almost always very clean.
Bleu clair / Incolore à bleu-vert pâle s: Light blue / Colorless to pale blue-green depending on the axis (weak to moderate).
Spectre du fer, souvent peu net : bande: Iron spectrum, often indistinct: a weak band near 537 nm and near 456 nm.
Presque toujours très propre. Fins tubes: Almost always very clean. Fine tubes parallel to the axis (rain-like appearance), sometimes liquid cavities, feathers and fractures.
No notable reaction to a magnet.
Résine fossile d'arbres vieux de plusieu: Fossil resin from trees tens of millions of years old, yellow to orange, sometimes with trapped insects. Very light: it floats in salt water.
Isotrope, avec une anomalie de biréfring: Isotropic, with anomalous birefringence caused by internal strain.
Bulles d'air, débris végétaux, parfois d: Air bubbles, plant debris, sometimes insects, and circular fractures called "sun spangles" (tension discs).
Croix noire déformée par les tensions (a: Black cross distorted by strain (anomalous birefringence).
Un quartz violet, variété courante mais: A purple quartz: a common variety but always appreciated.
Violet / Rougeâtre-violet selon l'axe d': Purple / Reddish purple depending on the viewing axis (weak).
Aucune fluorescence notable sous UV long: No notable fluorescence under long-wave UV.
Aucune fluorescence notable sous UV cour: No notable fluorescence under short-wave UV.
Figure d'interférence uniaxiale visible: Uniaxial interference figure visible in convergent light.
Quartz bicolore montrant à la fois les t: A bicolor quartz showing both the purple of amethyst and the yellow-orange of citrine in the same crystal, coming almost exclusively from a single Bolivian deposit.
Violet / Jaune selon la zone et l'axe d': Purple / Yellow depending on the zone and the viewing axis (variable).
Zonation de couleur nette en secteurs, l: Sharp color zoning in sectors, the transition boundary between the two hues sometimes visible.
Une pierre à très fort trichroïsme (vert: A stone with very strong trichroism (green, red, yellow-brown depending on the angle).
Vert / Rouge / Jaune-brun selon les troi: Green / Red / Yellow-brown along the three axes (extremely strong).
Un phosphate bleu-vert, tendre et souven: A blue-green phosphate, soft and often mistaken for other stones (hence its name, from the Greek for "to deceive").
Blue / Yellow-green depending on the axis (moderate).
Fluorescence jaune à mauve possible sous: Yellow to mauve fluorescence possible under long-wave UV.
Weak or absent under short-wave UV.
Spectre des terres rares (didyme) : une: Rare-earth (didymium) spectrum: one thin band, with a sharp cut-off, in the yellow-orange (580-587 nm), and weak lines in the green (521 nm). It is rare in other blue stones.
Nombreuses inclusions et fractures, pier: Many inclusions and fractures, generally an included stone.
Un béryl d'un bleu profond, de type maxi: A deep blue beryl of the maxixe type: its color comes from natural color centers and fades in light. Much stronger than aquamarine.
Bleu profond / Incolore à bleu très pâle: Deep blue / Colorless to very pale blue depending on the axis (very strong).
Bandes dans le rouge et l'orangé vers 69: Bands in the red and orange near 695 nm and 628 nm, weaker near 550 nm.
Généralement propre, parfois des tubes p: Generally clean, sometimes tubes parallel to the axis and liquid cavities.
Variété rouge framboise du béryl, coloré: Raspberry-red variety of beryl, colored by traces of manganese, among the rarest gems in the world and almost never exceeding one carat once cut.
Dichroïsme faible à modéré entre rouge p: Weak to moderate dichroism between purplish red and orange depending on the axis.
Bandes d'absorption liées au manganèse,: Absorption bands linked to manganese, notably in the yellow-green.
Voiles de croissance et canaux allongés: Growth veils and occasional elongated channels, typical of beryls. Large gem-quality stones are rarely found.
Figure uniaxe centrée en lumière converg: Centered uniaxial figure in convergent light.
Aucune réaction marquée au filtre Chelse: No marked reaction to the Chelsea filter.
Cubic zirconia (CZ) : un simulant synthé: Cubic zirconia (CZ): a synthetic diamond simulant, cheap but physically very different.
Même réaction qu'aux UV courts, mais plu: Same reaction as under short-wave UV, but weaker, or no reaction.
Généralement très propre, poussières de: Generally very clean, polishing dust possible on the surface.
Le carbonate de calcium : tendre, clivab: Calcium carbonate: soft, cleavable into perfect rhombohedra, with a clear doubling of the image (double refraction). It fizzes in acid.
Rouge, rose ou orangé (manganèse), parfo: Red, pink or orange (manganese), sometimes blue or white, depending on the specimen.
Stronger in short wave, red to pink.
Clivage rhomboédrique parfait, plans de: Perfect rhombohedral cleavage, polysynthetic twin planes, two-phase cavities.
Un sulfate de strontium d'un bleu pâle c: A strontium sulfate of a pale sky blue. Fragile and cleavable, it is kept as a crystal or fragment rather than cut.
Clivages parfaits, inclusions liquides,: Perfect cleavages, liquid inclusions, small crystals of sulfur or calcite.
Une pierre jaune-vert extrêmement dure,: An extremely hard yellow-green stone, the third hardest mineral after corundum and diamond.
Yellow / Pale green depending on the axis (weak).
Spectre du fer : une bande centrée à 444: Iron spectrum: a band centered at 444 nm, in the blue-violet. Useful to tell yellow to green chrysoberyl from brown sapphires.
Cristaux maclés en \"roue\", fines inclu: Twinned crystals in a "wheel" pattern, fine liquid inclusions.
La variété à changement de couleur du ch: The color-change variety of chrysoberyl: green in daylight, red under incandescent light.
Vert / Orange / Rouge selon les trois ax: Green / Orange / Red along the three axes (very strong).
Spectre du chrome : le violet et le bleu: Chromium spectrum: violet and blue are absorbed, as well as a band in the yellow-orange (550-605 nm); often a single line in the red (680-684 nm), sometimes weak lines near 645 and 655 nm. Depending on the color, the width and position of the lines change slightly.
Quartz jaune à orangé, dont la grande ma: Yellow to orange quartz, most of the commercial material coming from the heat treatment of amethyst.
Jaune pâle / Jaune plus soutenu selon l': Pale yellow / Deeper yellow depending on the axis (weak).
Zonation de couleur en bandes parallèles: Color zoning in parallel bands, occasional veils of fine fissures.
Squelette calcaire d'une colonie de poly: Calcareous skeleton of a colony of polyps (Corallium): magnesian calcite in fine rods, from pale pink to blood red. It effervesces in contact with an acid.
Inerte à rose pâle faible selon la teint: Inert to weak pale pink depending on the hue.
Agrégat opaque de calcite : pas de lectu: Opaque calcite aggregate: no usable optical reading.
Fines stries parallèles et motif ondulé: Fine parallel striations and wavy pattern of the skeleton, small round pores.
Un corindon rouge intense, envoyé pour c: A deep red corundum, sent in to confirm whether it is a natural ruby.
Rouge / Orangé-rouge selon l'axe d'obser: Red / Orange-red depending on the viewing axis.
Rouge vif (chrome). Naturel ou synthétiq: Bright red (chromium). Natural or synthetic: the reaction is the same.
Spectre du chrome : raies fines dans le: Chromium spectrum: fine lines in the red (694, 668 and 659 nm), a broad band swallowing the yellow-green (510-600 nm), the violet strongly absorbed and two iron lines in the blue (468 and 476 nm). The 694 nm line may look double or shine like an emission line.
Soie de rutile (inclusions aciculaires),: Rutile silk (needle-like inclusions), sometimes halos around crystals.
Corindon rouge obtenu par fusion de poud: Red corundum obtained by melting alumina powder; identical in appearance to a ruby, its production dates back to the early 20th century.
Spectre du chrome : raies fines dans le: Chromium spectrum: fine lines in the red (694, 668 and 659 nm) and a broad band in the yellow-green. The iron lines in the blue (468 and 476 nm) are missing: a synthetic ruby contains none.
Bulles de gaz sphériques ou en forme de: Spherical or comma-shaped gas bubbles, sometimes aligned; curved, concentric growth striae.
Rouge à rouge très vif (chrome), comme l: Red to very bright red (chromium), like natural ruby.
Corindon bleu obtenu par fusion de poudr: Blue corundum obtained by melting alumina powder and coloring oxides; long used in watchmaking and cheap jewelry.
Bleu / Bleu-violacé selon l'axe d'observ: Blue / Violet-blue depending on the viewing axis.
Bulles de gaz sphériques, stries de croi: Spherical gas bubbles, curved concentric growth striae, no natural mineral inclusion at all.
Généralement vert foncé, comme le saphir: Generally dark green, like natural blue sapphire.
Une calcédoine orange à rouge sang, colo: An orange to blood-red chalcedony, colored by iron oxide. Translucent and vitreous, it is polished as a cabochon; it is often heated to make it redder.
Fines bandes de couleur, nuages d'oxyde: Fine color bands, clouds of iron oxide; fibrous chalcedony structure.
Kératine compactée formant la corne du r: Compacted keratin forming the horn of the rhinoceros, chemically close to human hair and nails, unrelated to ivory. Demand on illegal markets, fueled by medicinal beliefs with no scientific basis, makes it one of the most poached materials in the world. Its sale is prohibited by CITES.
Structure fibreuse compacte, visible sou: Compact fibrous structure, visible as fine fibers parallel to the base of the horn.
Dent canine spiralée du narval, cétacé a: Spiral canine tooth of the narwhal, an Arctic whale sometimes nicknamed the "unicorn of the sea". Its sale is regulated by CITES to protect the species.
Ivoire crème, marqué de sillons en spira: Cream ivory, marked with spiral grooves
Fluorescence blanc-bleuté sous UV longue: Bluish white fluorescence under long-wave UV.
Uniaxe (biréfringent), lecture diffuse t: Uniaxial (doubly refractive), diffuse reading typical of an organic aggregate.
Croissance en spirale senestre caractéri: Characteristic left-handed spiral growth, visible as twisted striations over the whole length.
Une pierre incolore à l'éclat exceptionn: A colorless stone of exceptional brilliance, sent in for authentication.
Réaction variable, nulle à forte. Le ble: Variable reaction, none to strong. Blue is the most common reaction; green and yellow too.
Généralement une fluorescence plus faibl: Generally weaker fluorescence than under long-wave UV.
Spectre variable selon le type ; raies d: Spectrum varies with the type; lines in the violet possible (Cape series).
Inclusions cristallines sombres possible: Dark crystalline inclusions possible, generally few.
Diamant de synthèse obtenu par dépôt chi: Synthetic diamond obtained by chemical vapor deposition: carbon atoms settle layer by layer on a diamond seed placed in a hydrocarbon plasma.
Généralement très propre ; fin grainage: Generally very clean; fine graining parallel to the growth layers sometimes visible at high magnification.
Diamant de synthèse obtenu par haute pre: Synthetic diamond obtained at high pressure and high temperature, reproducing in a few weeks the conditions in which natural diamond forms, using a metal catalyst.
Généralement très propre ; rares inclusi: Generally very clean; rare residual metallic inclusions from the growth catalyst possible.
Légère réaction possible avec un aimant: Slight reaction possible with a very strong magnet (residual metallic inclusions from the growth process).
Un diopside vert intense coloré par le c: An intense green diopside colored by chromium, often cut into small stones.
Vert jaunâtre / Vert bleuté selon l'axe: Yellowish green / Bluish green depending on the axis (strong).
Fines inclusions fibreuses, parfois stru: Fine fibrous inclusions, sometimes a "feather" structure.
Modérément attiré par un aimant puissant: Moderately attracted to a strong magnet (iron-magnesium silicate).
Kératine translucide provenant de la car: Translucent keratin from the shell of the hawksbill turtle, shaped since antiquity into jewelry, combs and inlays for its unique mottled pattern. Its sale has been banned by CITES since 1977 to protect this species, now critically endangered.
Zones pigmentées irrégulières emprisonné: Irregular pigmented zones trapped in a homogeneous translucent matrix.
Un béryl vert, coloré par le chrome (et: A green beryl, colored by chromium (and sometimes vanadium): emerald. Brittle despite its hardness, it is almost always fractured and carries its "garden" inclusions.
Bleu-vert / Jaune-vert selon l'axe d'obs: Bluish green / Yellowish green depending on the viewing axis (weak to pronounced).
Spectre du chrome : bandes dans le rouge: Chromium spectrum: bands in the red that are sharper on one side than the other (absorption from orange to red, 590-630 nm), fine lines near 664 and 683 nm. Absorption in the orange up to the yellow can be very weak. No obvious line in the blue.
Inclusions en \"jardin\" : cavités à plu: "Garden" inclusions: multi-phase cavities, fissures, mica flakes; they change with the mine.
Rouge vif ou rose à verdâtre, naturelle: Bright red or pink to greenish, natural or synthetic. The intensity depends on the chromium content.
Une fluorite violette, minéral tendre et: A purple fluorite, a soft and fragile mineral whose name gave the word "fluorescence". Almost all colors exist, except red and black.
Bleue ou verte, parfois marquée. Peut ne: Blue or green, sometimes strong. May show no reaction.
Moins marquée. Peut ne présenter aucune: Less marked. May show no reaction.
Deux et trois phases, clivages et inclus: Two- and three-phase inclusions, cleavages and solid inclusions such as pyrite. Color and growth zones are not rare. The perfect octahedral cleavage can leave conchoidal fractures.
Une fluorite zonée, veinée de bandes vio: A zoned fluorite, veined with purple, green, white or pinkish bands. Every cut stone shows a different pattern.
Une fluorite d'un bleu profond, tendre e: A deep blue fluorite, soft and fragile, with perfect octahedral cleavage.
Le Blue John : une fluorite à bandes vio: Blue John: a fluorite with purple, white and yellow bands, specific to one English deposit. Very fragile, it is impregnated with resin before being cut.
Bandes de couleur violettes, blanches et: Purple, white and yellow color bands; many cavities and cleavages. Resin impregnation is common before cutting.
Une fluorite jaune à jaune doré, tendre: A yellow to golden-yellow fluorite, soft and fragile. It looks like citrine but scratches very easily.
Une fluorite verte, tendre et fragile. P: A green fluorite, soft and fragile. Almost all colors exist in fluorite, except red and black.
Grenat de gadolinium-gallium synthétique: Synthetic gadolinium gallium garnet, a diamond simulant of very high density but relatively soft, rare in jewelry today.
Généralement très propre, rares bulles d: Generally very clean, rare round gas bubbles.
Le béryl incolore : goshénite est le nom: Colorless beryl: goshenite is the name given to a beryl with no color, the purest variety of the group.
Un grenat rouge sombre, à ne pas confond: A dark red garnet, not to be confused with a ruby or a spinel.
Spectre du fer : le jaune est absorbé (b: Iron spectrum: yellow is absorbed (band from 577 to 594 nm), with thinner bands in the mid green and blue-green (505 and 530 nm). In dark or large stones these bands may merge; weak bands in the orange and blue are also noted.
Cristaux d'apatite ou de zircon entourés: Apatite or zircon crystals surrounded by halos, frequent internal fissures.
Grisâtre à rouge foncé : pas de rouge vi: Grayish to dark red: no bright red (pyrope-almandine).
Fortement attiré par un aimant puissant: Strongly attracted to a strong magnet (high iron content).
Un grenat vert à très fort éclat, l'un d: A green garnet of very high luster, one of the most prized of the garnet family.
Forte absorption dans le violet et le bl: Strong absorption in the violet and blue, transparency in the green.
Attiré par un aimant puissant (grenat ri: Attracted to a strong magnet (iron-rich garnet).
Un grenat brun-orangé (\"cinnamon stone\: A brown-orange garnet ("cinnamon stone"), not to be confused with spessartite.
Aspect interne \"mélasse\" (treacle) car: Characteristic "treacle" internal appearance, growth swirls visible under the microscope.
Faible réaction à l'aimant (moins de fer: Weak reaction to a magnet (less iron than almandine).
Variété massive et hydratée de grenat gr: Massive, hydrated variety of grossular garnet, sometimes nicknamed "Transvaal jade" because of its resemblance to jade.
Bande d'absorption diffuse liée au chrom: Diffuse absorption band linked to chromium or iron depending on the hue.
Petits cristaux noirs opaques (oxydes) d: Small opaque black crystals (oxides) scattered through the mass, compact granular texture.
Légère réaction possible avec un aimant: Slight reaction possible with a very strong magnet (traces of iron).
Grenat de couleur orange à rose-orangé,: Garnet of orange to pinkish-orange color, intermediate between pyrope and spessartite, long considered a reject before being recognized as a variety in its own right.
Bandes d'absorption du fer et du manganè: Combined iron and manganese absorption bands.
Cristaux d'apatite ou de zircon entourés: Apatite or zircon crystals surrounded by halos, occasional internal fissures.
Modérément attiré par un aimant puissant: Moderately attracted to a strong magnet (intermediate iron content).
Un grenat rouge profond, plus léger et d: A deep red garnet, lighter and with a lower RI than almandine.
Parfois des cristaux de rutile en aiguil: Sometimes needle-like rutile crystals, generally few.
Modérément attiré par un aimant puissant: Moderately attracted to a strong magnet (iron and magnesium).
Grenat rouge-violacé (\"framboise\"), in: Purplish-red garnet ("raspberry"), intermediate between pyrope and almandine.
Attiré par un aimant puissant (teneur en: Attracted to a strong magnet (intermediate iron content).
Un grenat orangé vif, à ne pas confondre: A vivid orange garnet, not to be confused with red almandine.
Attiré par un aimant puissant (fer et ma: Attracted to a strong magnet (iron and manganese).
Un grenat vert vif, rare et recherché, à: A vivid green garnet, rare and sought after, not to be confused with emerald or peridot.
Fibres d'amphibole, inclusions caractéri: Amphibole fibers, inclusions characteristic of East African deposits.
Réaction rougeâtre possible si coloré au: Reddish reaction possible if colored by chromium.
Aucune réaction notable à l'aimant (gren: No notable reaction to a magnet (iron-poor garnet).
Le grenat vert émeraude du chrome. Il ne: The emerald-green chromium garnet. It forms only tiny crystals packed into a sparkling crust: it is kept as a druse, never as a cut stone.
Spectre du chrome : raies fines vers 690: Chromium spectrum: fine lines near 690 nm.
Druse de minuscules cristaux ; pas de cr: Druse of tiny crystals; no crystals large enough for cutting.
Un sulfate de calcium hydraté, le minéra: A hydrated calcium sulfate, the mineral of plaster: it can be scratched with a fingernail. White, silky or pearly, it is not cut and is kept as a piece.
Clivages parfaits, aspect fibreux ou mas: Perfect cleavages, fibrous or massive appearance; needles and flakes.
Un béryl jaune citron à jaune doré foncé: A lemon-yellow to dark golden-yellow beryl, colored by iron. It can also be obtained by irradiating a green or blue beryl.
Jaune pâle / Jaune doré selon l'axe (fai: Pale yellow / Golden yellow depending on the axis (weak).
Inclusions en \"pluie\" : fins tubes par: "Rain" inclusions: fine tubes parallel to the crystal axis, sometimes liquid cavities and "fingerprint" fissures.
Un oxyde de fer opaque à éclat métalliqu: An opaque iron oxide with metallic luster, often cut as a cabochon rather than faceted.
Non applicable (minéral opaque à éclat m: Not applicable (opaque mineral with metallic luster).
Légèrement attiré par un aimant puissant: Slightly attracted to a strong magnet (iron oxide, a much weaker reaction than a truly ferromagnetic mineral).
La variété transparente de la cordiérite: The transparent variety of cordierite: a blue-violet stone with strong trichroism, sometimes called the Vikings' stone. Rarely colorless; the material is fragile.
Bleu / Violet / Jaune pâle selon les tro: Blue / Violet / Pale yellow along the three axes (very strong: the base color can change completely with the viewing direction).
Deux bandes dans le jaune, une bande étr: Two bands in the yellow, a narrow band in the green and three bands in the blue and violet; varies with the viewing direction.
Minces plaquettes de magnétite et d'oxyd: Thin platelets of magnetite and iron oxide, sometimes in large numbers; wavy fissures and healing feathers common. Twin planes possible.
Une iolite parsemée de plaquettes d'héma: An iolite scattered with reddish hematite platelets: they give an aventurescence effect and sometimes a pseudo cat's eye. The variety is called "bloodshot".
Bleu / Violet / Jaune pâle selon les tro: Blue / Violet / Pale yellow along the three axes (strong trichroism).
Innombrables plaquettes d'hématite rouge: Countless reddish hematite platelets: they give an aventurescence effect and sometimes a pseudo cat's eye. Wavy fissures and healing feathers common.
Dentine provenant des défenses d'éléphan: Dentine from elephant tusks. Its international trade has been banned by the Washington Convention (CITES) since 1989 because of the massive poaching that decimated elephant populations.
Fluorescence bleu-blanc caractéristique: Characteristic bluish-white fluorescence under long-wave UV.
Fluorescence plus faible et diffuse sous: Weaker, diffuse fluorescence under short-wave UV.
Aucun spectre d'absorption caractéristiq: No characteristic absorption spectrum with the spectroscope.
En coupe transversale, fines lignes entr: In cross-section, fine crossing lines (Schreger lines) forming angles generally greater than 115°.
Dentine issue des canines et incisives d: Dentine from the canines and incisors of the hippopotamus, known for its hardness and very fine grain, once used to make dentures before synthetic materials appeared. Like elephant ivory, its international trade is banned by CITES.
Cireux, prenant un poli particulièrement: Waxy, taking a particularly fine polish
Grain exceptionnellement fin et homogène: Exceptionally fine, uniform grain, without marked crossing structure.
Dentine fossile extraite des défenses de: Fossil dentine taken from the tusks of woolly mammoths preserved in the Siberian permafrost for millennia. Unlike elephant ivory, its sale is legal in most countries because the species is extinct, which sadly feeds a parallel trade in fresh ivory falsely labeled.
Beige à brun, parfois taché de bleu-vert: Beige to brown, sometimes stained blue-green
Fluorescence bleu-blanc plus faible et i: Weaker, irregular bluish-white fluorescence under long-wave UV.
Lignes de Schreger entrecroisées formant: Crossing Schreger lines forming angles generally smaller than 115°, often with surface cracks due to ageing.
Dentine provenant des défenses de morse,: Dentine from walrus tusks, recognizable by its characteristic granular core in cross-section. Its sale is heavily regulated and banned in many countries to protect Arctic populations.
Cœur central granuleux et marbré, nettem: Granular, marbled central core, clearly distinct from the dense outer layer, visible in cross-section.
Fin réseau de petits pores, sans lignes: Fine network of small pores, no Schreger lines; regular cellular structure visible with a loupe.
Silicate de sodium et d'aluminium du gro: Sodium aluminum silicate of the pyroxene group, the more prized of the two varieties of "jade".
Anisotrope, biaxial (biréfringent), lect: Anisotropic, biaxial (doubly refractive), diffuse reading typical of a polycrystalline aggregate.
Spectre du fer : une raie fine à 437 nm,: Iron spectrum: a fine line at 437 nm, in the blue-violet, whatever the color of the specimen (even pale).
Texture grenue à fibreuse entrelacée typ: Granular to interlocked fibrous texture typical of a compact crystalline aggregate.
Silicate de calcium et de magnésium du g: Calcium magnesium silicate of the amphibole group (tremolite-actinolite series), the most widespread variety of "jade".
Broad absorption band linked to iron.
Structure feutrée de fibres entrelacées,: Felted structure of interlocking fibers, giving the aggregate exceptional toughness.
Un bois fossile devenu lignite, d'un noi: A fossil wood turned into lignite, deep black, warm to the touch and light. It is polished into cabochons and carved; heated with a needle, it smells of coal.
Opaque : aucune lecture optique en lumiè: Opaque: no optical reading in transmitted light.
Cassure conchoïdale, parfois fibres de b: Conchoidal fracture, sometimes fossil wood fibers; no visible pores.
Aucune réaction notable à l'aimant ; s'é: No notable reaction to a magnet; becomes electrified by rubbing.
Une pierre rose-violet pâle, sensible à: A pale pink-violet stone, sensitive to prolonged light (risk of fading).
Rose intense / Incolore selon l'axe d'ob: Intense pink / Colorless depending on the viewing axis (strong).
Clivage net dans une direction, fracture: Sharp cleavage in one direction, parallel fractures possible.
Silicate d'aluminium au port cristallin: Aluminum silicate with an elongated bladed crystal habit, known for a hardness that varies strongly with the direction tested.
Vitreux à nacré sur les plans de clivage: Vitreous to pearly on cleavage planes
Incolore / Bleu pâle / Bleu soutenu selo: Colorless / Pale blue / Deep blue along the three axes (strong).
Fine absorption lines linked to iron.
Plans de clivage marqués, zonation de co: Marked cleavage planes, color zoning in bands along the length of the crystal.
Feldspath plagioclase montrant un jeu de: Plagioclase feldspar showing an iridescent play of light (labradorescence) caused by an internal lamellar structure.
Fines lamelles internes responsables du: Fine internal lamellae responsible for the characteristic iridescent play of light.
Roche d'un bleu profond, faite de lazuri: Deep blue rock made of lazurite with white calcite and flecks of golden pyrite: the blue stone of the pharaohs.
Inerte, parfois rose-orangé dans la calc: Inert, sometimes pink-orange in the calcite.
Agrégat opaque (roche) : lecture diffuse: Opaque aggregate (rock): diffuse reading of lazurite, isotropic.
Pas de spectre net ; absorption large da: No clear spectrum; broad absorption in the yellow-orange.
Paillettes de pyrite dorée et veines de: Flecks of golden pyrite and veins of white calcite in the blue mass of lazurite.
Aucune réaction (rougeâtre pour certaine: No reaction (reddish for some dyed imitations).
Un carbonate de cuivre vert, rubané en c: A green copper carbonate, banded in concentric circles of light and dark greens. Opaque and soft, it is polished as a cabochon or into beads; it effervesces in acid.
Bandes concentriques vert clair et vert: Concentric light green and dark green bands, silky fibrous texture; botryoidal cavities.
Carbure de silicium synthétique, un autr: Synthetic silicon carbide, another diamond simulant, but doubly refractive unlike diamond.
Anisotrope, uniaxial (biréfringent) — dé: Anisotropic, uniaxial (doubly refractive) — doubling of the facet edges sometimes visible at high magnification.
Généralement très propre, inclusions mét: Generally very clean, rare metallic inclusions.
Un verre naturel vert bouteille, né de l: A bottle-green natural glass, born from a meteorite impact fifteen million years ago. Rough, its surface is sculpted with folds; it is faceted into a bottle-green stone.
Fines bulles sphériques, filaments de ve: Fine spherical bubbles, silica glass filaments (lechatelierite), flow structure; sculpted surface.
Un béryl rose pêche à rosé, coloré par l: A peach-pink to rosy beryl, colored by manganese. It is often heated to obtain a pure pink.
Rose / Rose bleuté selon l'axe (faible à: Pink / Bluish pink depending on the axis (weak to moderate).
Tubes parallèles à l'axe (aspect de plui: Tubes parallel to the axis (rain-like appearance), elongated liquid inclusions and growth veils.
Verre volcanique naturel formé par un re: Natural volcanic glass formed by very rapid cooling of silica-rich lava, with no crystalline structure.
Cassure conchoïdale caractéristique, par: Characteristic conchoidal fracture, sometimes gas bubbles or flake-like mineral inclusions.
Un verre volcanique noir piqué de taches: A black volcanic glass dotted with radiating white patches, like flakes: spherules of cristobalite. It is polished as a cabochon.
Sphérulites blanches de cristobalite en: White spherulites of cristobalite in sprays, in a black glass; conchoidal fracture.
Quartz fibreux brun doré : les fibres de: Golden-brown fibrous quartz: the crocidolite fibers were replaced by quartz and iron oxides, giving a mobile silky reflection, chatoyancy.

Silice hydratée amorphe de couleur orang: Amorphous hydrated silica of orange to bright red color, generally without play of color.

Nuances marquées de brun-rouge, orangé e: Strong shades of red-brown, orange and dark brown depending on the viewing axis.

Spectre du fer : triplet de bandes dans: Iron spectrum: a triplet of bands in the blue to blue-green (451, 470 and 494 nm), sharpest at 494 nm. If the absorption is weak, the light must be adjusted; in some stones the bands merge into a single broad band.
Petites fractures discoïdes en forme de: Small disc-shaped fractures around included crystals.
Légèrement attiré par un aimant puissant: Slightly attracted to a strong magnet (moderate iron content).
Perle de nacre formée autour d'un noyau: Nacre pearl formed around a nucleus in a farmed oyster: calcium carbonate arranged in layers, with a soft, pearly luster.

Perle de culture d'une huître à lèvres n: Cultured pearl from a black-lipped oyster of Polynesia: gray to black, with green, blue or aubergine overtones; it is sometimes treated to give it a "chocolate" hue.
Inerte à rouge-brun faible, caractéristi: Inert to weak red-brown, characteristic of natural color.
Absorption diffuse ; une bande vers 700: Diffuse absorption; a band near 700 nm in pearls of natural color.
Lignes de croissance, petites cernes et: Growth lines, small rings and surface pits; mother-of-pearl nucleus visible on X-rays.
Un béryl au césium rose à rougeâtre, tra: A pink to reddish cesium beryl, translucent to transparent, discovered only in 2002 in Madagascar. It is trigonal and grows in tabular rhombohedral crystals, heavily included. Fragile despite its hardness of 8.
Rose orangé moyen / Rose violacé à viole: Medium orange-pink / Purplish pink to pink-violet (dichroic).
Une bande dans le bleu-vert vers 494 nm: A band in the blue-green near 494 nm and a smaller one in the green near 563 nm.
Matériau généralement très inclus : tube: Generally heavily included material: growth tubes and healing feathers. May be resin-impregnated.
Feldspar alcalin montrant un phénomène d: Alkali feldspar showing a bluish floating light effect (adularescence) caused by the intergrowth of two minerals.
Structure lamellaire fine en intercroiss: Fine lamellar intergrowth structure, responsible for the characteristic bluish floating glow.
Quartz vert, rare à l'état naturel, la m: Green quartz, rare in nature, most of the commercial material being obtained by heat treatment of amethyst.
Vert pâle / Vert plus soutenu selon l'ax: Pale green / Deeper green depending on the axis (weak).
Un silicate d'un vert tendre qui rappell: A soft green silicate that recalls an apple, translucent, with pearly reflections. It is polished mostly as a cabochon.
Agrégats fibreux rayonnants en gerbes, p: Radiating fibrous aggregates in sprays, small cavities, finely granular appearance.
Sulfure de fer opaque à éclat métallique: Opaque iron sulfide with a golden metallic luster, nicknamed "fool's gold".
Aucune réaction notable à l'aimant, malg: No notable reaction to a magnet, despite its iron content.
Un cristal de quartz incolore, courant,: A common colorless quartz crystal, sent in for a first examination.
Généralement très propre, parfois inclus: Generally very clean, sometimes fluid or feather inclusions.
Quartz brun-gris, coloré par des centres: Gray-brown quartz, colored by aluminum-related color centers activated by natural background irradiation.
Brun clair / Brun plus soutenu selon l'a: Light brown / Deeper brown depending on the axis (weak).
Zonation de couleur diffuse, voiles de f: Diffuse color zoning, occasional veils of fine fissures.
Quartz rose, souvent riche en inclusions: Pink quartz, often rich in fibrous rutile inclusions that can produce an asterism effect.
Rose pâle / Rose plus soutenu selon l'ax: Pale pink / Deeper pink depending on the axis (very weak).
Fines inclusions fibreuses abondantes, v: Abundant fine fibrous inclusions, dense veils giving a milky appearance.
Carbonate de manganèse rose à rouge, sou: Pink to red manganese carbonate, often shown in concentric bands, nicknamed the "Inca rose".
Rose pâle / Rose plus soutenu selon l'ax: Pale pink / Deeper pink depending on the axis (weak).
Bandes concentriques alternant teintes c: Concentric bands alternating light and deep hues, very characteristic.
Silicate de manganèse rose, généralement: Pink manganese silicate, generally crossed by black veins of manganese oxides.
Veines noires d'oxydes de manganèse serp: Black veins of manganese oxides snaking through the pink mass, very characteristic.
Légère réaction possible avec un aimant: Slight reaction possible with a very strong magnet (traces of manganese).
Un corindon bleu intense, envoyé pour co: A deep blue corundum, sent in to confirm whether it is a natural sapphire.
Bleu / Bleu-vert selon l'axe d'observati: Blue / Blue-green depending on the viewing axis (strong).
Saphir naturel : aucune réaction, parfoi: Natural sapphire: no reaction, sometimes a weak green.
Spectre du fer : une raie fine ou une mi: Iron spectrum: a fine line or a thin band in the blue, near 450 nm. Some pale blue sapphires show more than one; synthetic (Verneuil) sapphires show none.
Soie de rutile, zonation de couleur en b: Rutile silk, color zoning in hexagonal bands.
Corindon dépourvu d'éléments traces colo: Corundum with none of the coloring trace elements; historically used as a cheap substitute for diamond.
Généralement très propre, quelques crist: Generally very clean, a few scattered fine crystals possible.
Corindon jaune, couleur due à des centre: Yellow corundum, its color due to color centers or traces of iron.
Bande d'absorption diffuse dans le bleu-: Diffuse absorption band in the blue-violet.
Zonation de couleur en bandes hexagonale: Color zoning in hexagonal bands, scattered fine crystals.
Corindon orange, teinte rare obtenue par: Orange corundum, a rare hue obtained through a particular balance between several trace elements.
Orange clair / Orangé plus soutenu selon: Light orange / Deeper orange depending on the axis (weak).

Zonation de couleur en bandes, cristaux: Color zoning in bands, scattered fine crystals.
Aucune réaction ou réaction rougeâtre tr: No reaction or very weak reddish reaction.
Corindon rose, coloré par de faibles tra: Pink corundum, colored by faint traces of chromium, on the stylistic border with ruby.
Rose clair / Rose plus soutenu selon l'a: Light pink / Deeper pink depending on the axis (moderate).
Raies d'absorption fines dans le vert, d: Fine absorption lines in the green, due to a chromophore element in low concentration.
Soie de rutile fine, légère zonation de: Fine rutile silk, light color zoning.
Réaction rougeâtre faible à modérée poss: Weak to moderate reddish reaction possible.
Corindon vert, souvent formé de fines ba: Green corundum, often made of fine alternating blue/yellow bands giving a green hue to the naked eye.
Vert / Jaune-vert selon l'axe d'observat: Green / Yellow-green depending on the viewing axis (strong).
Spectre du fer : trois bandes dans le bl: Iron spectrum: three bands in the blue (450, 460 and 471 nm). In very dark natural sapphires, the two widest bands may merge into one.
Zonation de couleur marquée en bandes fi: Marked color zoning in fine alternating bands, frequent internal fissures.
Corindon violet, couleur résultant de la: Purple corundum, a color resulting from the combination of several trace elements.
Violet-bleu / Violet-rouge selon l'axe d: Violet-blue / Violet-red depending on the viewing axis (moderate).
Bandes d'absorption combinées, larges et: Combined absorption bands, broad and diffuse.
Zonation de couleur en secteurs, cristau: Color zoning in sectors, scattered fine crystals.
Silicate d'aluminium de la série mariali: Aluminum silicate of the marialite-meionite series, with a characteristic elongated prismatic crystal habit.
Jaune pâle / Jaune plus soutenu selon l': Pale yellow / Deeper yellow depending on the axis (moderate).
Inclusions fibreuses ou tubulaires paral: Fibrous or tubular inclusions parallel to the elongation axis of the crystal.
La variété transparente du gypse : de gr: The transparent variety of gypsum: large clear crystals, cleavable into plates, with a pearly luster. So soft that it is not cut; it is kept as a crystal.
Clivages parfaits, lames minces, petites: Perfect cleavages, thin plates, small bubbles and liquid cavities; parallel striations.
Variété compacte et dure d'antigorite (g: Compact, hard variety of antigorite (serpentine group), sometimes sold as a substitute for jade.
Anisotrope, biaxial (biréfringent), lect: Anisotropic, biaxial (doubly refractive), diffuse reading typical of an aggregate.
Texture compacte à grain fin, parfois ve: Compact fine-grained texture, sometimes whitish veinlets.
Borate de magnésium et d'aluminium, long: A magnesium aluminum borate, long mistaken for brown peridot before being recognized as a distinct species in 1952.
Jaune pâle / Brun clair / Brun-rouge som: Pale yellow / Light brown / Dark red-brown along the three axes (strong).
Fine absorption bands linked to iron.
Généralement peu incluse, cristaux fins: Generally lightly included, occasional fine crystals.
Une roche d'un bleu profond, veinée de b: A deep blue rock veined with white, sometimes dotted with orange patches under the UV lamp. It looks like lapis lazuli, without the pyrite.
Plages orange à orange rouge, parfois in: Orange to red-orange patches, sometimes intense (hackmanite).
Orange, stronger than under long wave.
Veines blanches de calcite, masse bleue: White calcite veins, homogeneous blue mass; no pyrite, unlike lapis lazuli.
Un sulfure de zinc d'une dispersion près: A zinc sulfide with a dispersion nearly four times that of diamond: red, orange, brown or honey, with an almost metallic adamantine luster. Very soft and cleavable in six directions, it is cut with care.
Orange à jaune selon l'échantillon (mang: Orange to yellow depending on the specimen (manganese).
Aucun spectre d'absorption net ; la coul: No clear absorption spectrum; the color comes from iron.
Clivage dodécaédrique parfait dans six d: Perfect dodecahedral cleavage in six directions, twin planes, fine inclusions of pyrite and galena; very fiery appearance.
Une pierre de feu : sa dispersion dépass: A stone of fire: its dispersion exceeds that of diamond and it throws orange-red flashes on a greenish-yellow background. Soft for a gem, it is handled with care.
Jaune verdâtre à vert, brun miel: Greenish yellow to green, honey brown
Bandes fines du didyme (terres rares) ve: Fine didymium (rare-earth) bands near 580 nm in some stones.
Plans de macle, fissures, inclusions de: Twin planes, fissures, inclusions of rutile and apatite; doubled appearance caused by the strong birefringence (doubling of the facet edges).
Une pierre rouge vif, historiquement sou: A bright red stone, historically often mistaken for ruby.
Spectre du chrome : large bande qui abso: Chromium spectrum: a broad band that absorbs the green (520-585 nm) and several fine lines in the red (659, 668, 677 and 688 nm). The width and intensity of the bands vary; the number of red lines changes with the viewing conditions.
Réaction rouge à rosâtre, d'intensité mo: Red to pinkish reaction, of moderate intensity.
Une pierre bleu vif, à distinguer du sap: A bright blue stone, to be told apart from sapphire and blue zircon.
Spectre du cobalt : trois bandes dans le: Cobalt spectrum: three bands in the green (537 nm), the yellow-orange (585 nm) and the red-orange (632 nm), following each other "thin, thick, thick" from left to right. Their width varies with the depth of color and the size of the stone.
Le talc massif, la plus tendre des pierr: Massive talc, the softest of the ornamental stones: it can be scratched with a fingernail and carved with a knife. It feels greasy, gray-green to white.
Masse écailleuse très fine, parfois vein: Very fine scaly mass, sometimes veined with chlorite; soapy feel.
Un minéral d'une rareté extrême, découve: A mineral of extreme rarity, discovered in 1945 in a Dublin shop: pastel mauve, pink or violet, of great purity. Fine cut stones are almost impossible to find.
Mauve pâle / mauve rosé selon l'axe (fai: Pale mauve / pinkish mauve depending on the axis (weak).
Spectre faible : légère absorption du fe: Weak spectrum: slight iron absorption near 458 nm.
Généralement très propre ; de petites in: Generally very clean; small liquid inclusions, spinel and apatite crystals, rare healed fissures.
Une pierre bleu-violet, presque toujours: A blue-violet stone, almost always heat treated.
Bleu / Violet / Rouge-brun selon les tro: Blue / Violet / Red-brown along the three axes (very strong).
Généralement propre, parfois fines inclu: Generally clean, sometimes fine needle-like inclusions.
Un cristal synthétique cubique, d'une di: A cubic synthetic crystal with a dispersion more than four times that of diamond: an intense rainbow fire and dazzling brilliance. Soft, it scratches with wear. It can be any color.
Généralement très propre ; bulles de gaz: Generally very clean; occasional round gas bubbles, frequent polishing scratches.
Une topaze, de l'incolore au bleu Swiss: A topaz, from colorless to Swiss blue or imperial orange, very varied in color.
Incolore, bleu, jaune, orange ou rose: Colorless, blue, yellow, orange or pink
Faible : nuances proches de la couleur d: Weak: shades close to the body color depending on the axis.
Faible, jaunâtre à verdâtre selon la cou: Weak, yellowish to greenish depending on the color.

Tubes de croissance parallèles à l'axe,: Growth tubes parallel to the axis, fragmented liquid inclusions, fissures; color often zoned.
Une tourmaline bicolore : le rose d'un c: A bicolor tourmaline: pink on one side, green on the other, like the flesh and rind of a watermelon. Cut as a slice, it shows a pink heart, a white ring and a green border.
Rose / rose foncé d'un côté, vert / vert: Pink / dark pink on one side, green / dark green on the other depending on the axis (strong).
Partie rose : large absorption du vert v: Pink part: broad absorption of the green near 525 nm; green part: absorption of the red (iron) near 660 nm.
Tubes de croissance parallèles à l'axe (: Growth tubes parallel to the axis (rain-like appearance), fragmented liquid inclusions, fissures; sharply defined color zones, from pink to green, sometimes with a colorless ring.
Rose pâle dans la partie rose, vert tern: Pale pink in the pink part, dull green in the green part.
Une tourmaline cuprifère au bleu néon él: A copper-bearing tourmaline of electric neon blue, among the rarest and most expensive gems.
Bleu néon, vert bleuté ou violet: Neon blue, bluish green or violet
Bleu électrique / Bleu verdâtre selon l': Electric blue / Greenish blue depending on the viewing axis (strong).
Large bande d'absorption du cuivre dans: Broad copper absorption band in the red.
Inclusions liquides, tubes et fractures: Liquid inclusions, tubes and healed fractures; stones often heated.
Une tourmaline rose à rouge, variété app: A pink to red tourmaline, a variety called rubellite.
Rose clair / Rose foncé selon l'axe d'ob: Light pink / Dark pink depending on the viewing axis (weak to moderate).
Inclusions liquides fragmentées, fractur: Fragmented liquid inclusions, frequent internal fractures.
La tourmaline noire, la plus courante :: The black tourmaline, the most common: an iron boron silicate, deep black, opaque. Its crystals are deeply striated along their length.
Trop sombre pour voir le pléochroïsme :: Too dark to see pleochroism: very dark brown to black.
Pierre opaque : aucun spectre d'absorpti: Opaque stone: no usable absorption spectrum.
Fortes stries verticales sur les cristau: Strong vertical striations on the crystals, inclusions of quartz and feldspar in the host rock, fissures; the black hides almost every inclusion.
Faiblement attirée par un aimant puissan: Weakly attracted to a strong magnet (it contains iron).
Phosphate hydraté de cuivre et d'alumini: Hydrated copper aluminum phosphate, an opaque blue to green mineral used in jewelry since antiquity.
Fluorescence verdâtre à jaunâtre faible: Weak greenish to yellowish fluorescence possible under long-wave UV.
Veinules brunâtres ou noirâtres de matri: Brownish or blackish veinlets of host matrix frequent ("spider web").
Turquoise naturelle poreuse imprégnée de: Porous natural turquoise impregnated with resin to strengthen its structure and stabilize its color before cutting.
Fluorescence bleuâtre terne possible sou: Dull bluish fluorescence possible under long-wave UV (resin residues).
Veinules de matrice hôte, structure pore: Veinlets of host matrix, porous structure filled with a resinous substance.
Un verre imitant l'apparence d'une pierr: A glass imitating the look of a red gemstone.
Variable : peut présenter une surface bl: Variable: may show a chalky white surface.
Spectre continu sans raies nettes, ou ra: Continuous spectrum without sharp lines, or artificial lines depending on the dye.
Bulles rondes et stries d'écoulement, si: Round bubbles and flow striae, the typical signature of glass.
Grenat d'yttrium-aluminium synthétique,: Synthetic yttrium aluminum garnet, one of the first diamond simulants used in jewelry before the arrival of cubic zirconia (CZ).
Généralement très propre, bulles de gaz: Generally very clean, occasional round gas bubbles.
Un zircon bleu, souvent confondu avec le: A blue zircon, often mistaken for sapphire or blue spinel.
Dichroïsme faible à modéré selon la tein: Weak to moderate dichroism depending on the hue.
Anisotrope, uniaxial — biréfringence trè: Anisotropic, uniaxial — very high birefringence causing a visible doubling of the back facet edges.
Spectre de l'uranium : une raie nette da: Uranium spectrum: a sharp line in the red at 653 nm, accompanied by many other fine lines (590, 616, 660, 684 nm and in the green). Almost all zircons show them, even colorless ones; "metamict" stones (low zircons) have only diffuse bands.
Généralement propre ; dédoublement net d: Generally clean; clear doubling of the pavilion facets visible with a loupe.
Variété de zoïsite verte à brunâtre, chi: Green to brownish variety of zoisite, chemically related to tanzanite but lacking its famous blue-violet color.
Vert / Brun-jaune selon l'axe d'observat: Green / Yellow-brown depending on the viewing axis (strong).
Bandes d'absorption diffuses du fer et d: Combined diffuse absorption bands of iron and chromium.
Cristaux fins dispersés, parfois accompa: Scattered fine crystals, sometimes with fibrous inclusions.
Jadéite teintée (fer et chrome) : la rai: Dyed jadeite (iron and chromium): the 437 nm line, plus a weakly marked band, sometimes double, in the red (640-650 nm), due to chromium. Absorption in the violet and blue can be pronounced.
Verre au cobalt : les trois bandes sont: Cobalt glass: the three bands are spread wider than in spinel; the widest is in the red (660 nm). Under the Chelsea filter, red light passes, as in cobalt spinel.
Zircon traité par chauffage : une seule: Heat-treated zircon: a single fine line at 653 nm, sometimes another more diffuse line in the yellow and green. It is easier to see in light reflected from the stone's surface.
Verre rouge à l'or (colloïdal, « verre r: Gold red glass (colloidal, "gold ruby glass"): a single band in the green, from 510 to 555 nm, which may be diffuse; the lighting must be well controlled.
Verre rouge au sélénium : une forte marq: Selenium red glass: a strong bright-red mark, with complete absorption of everything that is not red up to about 625 nm, near 620 nm. No lines.
Verre rouge aux terres rares : le spectr: Rare-earth red glass: the rare-earth spectrum is superimposed on that of the glass; fine lines near 509, 573, 588 and 591 nm and a diffuse band in the green (520-555 nm). A pattern that helps tell glass from gems.
Saphir synthétique à changement de coule: Synthetic color-change sapphire (chromium and vanadium): a fine line in the blue at 475 nm, weakly marked and hard to see, a band in the yellow-green, and the red end absorbed.
Rouge : spinelle bleu synthétique, color: Red: synthetic blue spinel, colored with cobalt.
Certains spécimens teints en vert peuven: Some specimens dyed green may show a reddish or pinkish tint.
Rouge vif, orange-rosé ou rose : spinell: Bright red, orange-pink or pink: synthetic blue spinel, colored with cobalt.
Rose chair, ou incolore (topaze bleue ir: Flesh pink, or colorless (irradiated and heated blue topaz).
Verdâtre à vert de gris (verre bleu colo: Greenish to gray-green (blue glass colored by iron).
Généralement vert terne, quelquefois tei: Generally dull green, sometimes tinted with red.
Rouge intense à rose (quartz synthétique: Intense red to pink (cobalt-colored synthetic quartz).
La plupart des pierres présentent un ver: Most stones show a dull green.
Huit faces triangulaires (système cubiqu: Eight triangular faces (cubic system): the habit of diamond and spinel.
Octaèdre dont les faces portent des trig: An octahedron whose faces carry trigons: small triangular etch figures, sunken and inverted relative to the face. It is the typical surface mark of rough diamond.
Six faces carrées (système cubique) : la: Six square faces (cubic system): fluorite, pyrite; CVD synthetic diamond grows in cubic blocks.
Quatorze faces, six carrées et huit tria: Fourteen faces, six square and eight triangular: the shape of HPHT synthetic diamonds.
Douze faces en losange (système cubique): Twelve rhombus-shaped faces (cubic system): the typical habit of garnet.
Vingt-quatre faces en cerf-volant (systè: Twenty-four kite-shaped faces (cubic system): the second habit of garnets.
Prisme à six pans terminé par une face p: Six-sided prism ending in a flat face: beryls (emerald), apatite.
Prisme à six pans, strié, terminé en poi: Six-sided, striated prism ending in a point: quartz.
Deux pyramides à six faces accolées, en: Two six-faced pyramids joined together, barrel-shaped: sapphires.
Un long tonneau hexagonal aux extrémités: A long hexagonal barrel with stepped ends, striated across: the classic shape of rough sapphire.
Une bipyramide trapue, les pointes émous: A stocky bipyramid with blunted tips: a sapphire from a primary deposit.
Un prisme à six pans, trapu, aux extrémi: A stocky six-sided prism with flat or rhombohedral ends, frosted and dull: rough ruby.
Une plaque aplatie à six côtés, au bord: A flattened six-sided plate with a beveled edge: the rubies of Mong Hsu and Madagascar.
Un galet roulé par la rivière, arrondi,: A pebble rolled by the river, rounded, with worn faces: the gem gravels of Ceylon and Madagascar.
Un éclat anguleux aux grandes cassures p: An angular chip with large flat breaks, sometimes along the parting planes.
Deux octaèdres accolés et aplatis : une: Two octahedra joined and flattened: a triangular plate with truncated corners. It is the classic twin of spinel, which gave its name to the twin law.
Un octaèdre dont les six pointes sont co: An octahedron whose six points are cut by small square faces (the cube).
Un prisme hexagonal régulier, trapu : si: A regular, stocky hexagonal prism: six equal sides and two flat hexagonal faces at the ends (basal pinacoid).
Un prisme hexagonal régulier allongé dan: A regular hexagonal prism elongated along the growth axis: six equal sides, ending on each side in a flat hexagonal face (basal pinacoid).
Un long prisme hexagonal régulier, strié: A long regular hexagonal prism, striated along the axis, with both ends flat (basal pinacoid): the beryl "pencil".
Un court prisme hexagonal pointé aux deu: A short hexagonal prism pointed at both ends, like Herkimer diamonds: a crystal that grew free, without support.
Un long cristal fin à six pans, aux fine: A long, thin six-sided crystal with fine striations along the axis: aquamarine, emerald, apatite.
Un long prisme à section de triangle aux: A long prism with a triangular cross-section and rounded corners, deeply striated along its length: tourmaline.
Un prisme rectangulaire qui finit en coi: A rectangular prism ending in a wedge, striated along its length: topaz.
Prisme à section carrée terminé par une: A prism with a square cross-section ending in a pyramid: zircon.
Prisme à section rectangulaire ou losang: A prism with a rectangular or rhombic cross-section and oblique terminations: topaz, peridot, chrysoberyl.
Prisme aplati aux terminaisons obliques: A flattened prism with oblique terminations: spodumene (kunzite), feldspars, diopside.
Une croûte de minuscules cristaux serrés: A crust of tiny crystals packed on their rock, sparkling: the only form of uvarovite.
Une tranche mince coupée en travers du c: A thin slice cut across the crystal: a pink heart, a pale ring and a green border, for watermelon tourmaline.
Prisme à section triangulaire aux angles: A prism with a triangular cross-section and rounded corners, striated: tourmalines.
Un fragment d'octaèdre taillé par le cli: A fragment of octahedron cut by the perfect cleavage of fluorite: large flat faces, stair-step marks on the surface.
